title: Model comparison: who makes the wrong reward machines
eyebrow: reward machine generator and critic · models and thinking level · 2026-11-20
subtitle: Five generator and critic pairs, the thinking level of the production pair, and the two fixes that followed. Every wrong machine shows its task, LTLf and Reward Machine.

blocks.title: In plain words
blocks.text: The app turns a task in plain English into a Reward Machine in two steps: a generator model proposes rules, a critic model checks them. In production the generator is `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and the critic is `glm-5.3-flash`, both with reasoning set to `none`. With that pair, the three wrong machines have one cause: deepseek's first proposal is wrong and glm accepts it. Giving both models `medium` thinking, plus a critic wording fix and a card fix, makes all 46 test tasks come out right (46/46, against 42/46). A run then takes about 6 times longer.

items: **Who fails at `none`.** All 3 wrong machines of the production pair (W5a, U5, S2) are deepseek first proposals that glm accepted on its first call; a fourth task (O7) was accepted with redundant hard clauses. Swap either model and those cases come out right: Haiku + glm 6/6, deepseek + luna 6/6.

**Thinking fixes the generator.** U5, S2 and O7 are right in 3 of 3 runs at `medium`; W5a in 2 of 3. Thinking also makes glm a much better critic (22 of 28 wrong sets caught on call 1, against 14 of 28).

**A prompt rule clashed.** A strong critic (luna) looped on task G12 because two critic rules disagreed. One sentence in the critic prompt removed it: luna's G12 went from 7.33 rounds and 20 of 22 false alarms per run to 1 round and 0 of 2.
**Part of the "wrong" was the scorer.** On G12 the card did not list a machine that accepts exactly the same runs. A DFA equality proof added it: old G12 runs scored right go from 2/9 to 6/9.

**Limits.** One run per task in most rows, so single cases are single runs. The final 46/46 run (B4) changes three things at once (thinking, the critic wording, the card fix); the earlier `medium` run (m1) came before the critic wording and scored 19/20 on the hard cases and five random ones. The `none` rerun with the new wording was not run (budget). The CLI models think hard while the app default is `none`: arms compare a model plus its thinking, not a model alone.

**Later (loop 2).** A card audit made every stated order required (rescore: `none` 42 to 40 of 46, B4 stays 46). A sweep from `low` to `max` ends 46 of 46 at every level; `max` costs 4.5 times the `medium` wall time and doubles the short first proposals. Both sections sit before the open points; the sweep ran before the shape fix of `docs/paper/hidden-output-schema/`.

items: **Task cards.** 46 cards from `experiments/benchmark` in six groups (W, C, U, O, G, S; the S cards are local copies). Each card has the right clause sets. A machine is **right** when a card answer matches and no hard `Existence` sits on an earlier step; **accepted** when it matches only with such an extra `Existence`; **wrong** otherwise, or when the run ends with no machine.

**Hard subset (arms C and D).** W5a, U5, S2 and G12 (the cases A or B got wrong) plus U6, O5, G2, G7, G11 (random right ones), two runs each. Their right share is not comparable with A, B and E; compare case by case.

**CLI models.** The adapter calls Claude Code with `--safe-mode --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands --tools ""` and the app's system prompt; Haiku runs at `--effort max`. Codex runs with `--ignore-user-config --strict-config`, the app prompt as `model_instructions_file`, five instruction blocks and 14 features off; luna runs at `xhigh`. Checked on one call each: the Claude call carried 661 cache tokens instead of about 42 K, the Codex call 9.3 K input tokens instead of 23.5 K. No Codex flag removes `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, which is still sent as a user message. No call used a tool.

**Budget.** Final run limits were set to 130 OpenCode runs and 300 calls; the loop used 116 runs and 301 calls, one call over (a guard tripped after the last B4 run had started). Subscriptions never went above 30% of any window.

sections.title: Critic set: glm, luna and Haiku on the same items
sections.intro: The critic set has 38 items from the critic-clues loop: 28 wrong clause sets with 41 labelled defects, and 10 right ones. The critic reads one candidate at a time; a judge model (deepseek) says which defects its feedback names. Items w03 and r05 use UnlockPickup's events (a mechanical fix; they errored in the first report, which therefore had 36 items). The critic prompt is the old one for every row.

items: **First report, 36 items.** glm at `none` caught 13 of 27 wrong items on call 1 and flagged 20 of 40 defects; luna caught 26 of 27 and flagged 38 of 40. Both numbers reproduce from the copied records with `--items` on the same folders.

**By defect kind (flagged / labelled).** glm none: event 0/5, extra 1/7, missing 5/8, template 5/8. glm medium: event 3/5, extra 4/7, missing 6/8, template 7/8. luna and Haiku miss at most one per kind. glm at `medium` still accepts w01, w02, w04, w05, w10, w12, w16 and w22 with a defect left.

**What every strong critic rejects.** s02, w08 (W5a), w03, r05 and r10: they ask for orders the task states and the level forces (key before door, door before box). The cards mark those orders `forced`, so optional.

**Inside the pipeline.** glm caught 3 of 6 wrong first proposals of deepseek at `none`, and 11 of 12 at `medium` (4/5 in m1, 7/7 in B4); luna caught 5 of 5 in arm D. glm at `none` leaks its own reasoning into the feedback ("... holding_box)? No —", "wait, at_goal is soft").

blocks.text: Luna asks for too much. It rejected 24 of 71 right candidates in arm B and 25 of 41 in arm D, against glm's 4 of 46 in A and 0 of 18 in C. The cause on G12 is the prompt, shown in the fixes.

items: **Mistakes fixed by `medium`.** U5 (a soft `Precedence(door_open, key_lost)` for "try not to drop the key while the door is still closed"), S2 (the hard last step on the key, not the door), O7 (hard `Existence` of the ball and the key after glm's false alarm), and W5a in 2 of 3 runs.
**`high`.** One run, one case: right, at the same cost as `medium` on W5a (285 to 303 s and 22.7 K tokens at `medium`). One sample says nothing about `high`.

**New failure at `medium`: short first proposals.** In 10 of 66 `medium` runs (m1 plus B4) deepseek's first answer had fewer clauses than any card answer, often one clause. It never happened at `none` (0 of 46). The JSON was valid and the call had reasoned 1.4 to 4.6 K tokens, so the cause is unknown. glm at `medium` rejected all 10 and the second answer was right, so they cost a round, not a wrong machine.
**The price.** The same number of calls per run (2.35 against 2.39), about 6 times the wall time, and about 1,500 output tokens per call on average.

sections.title: Two fixes: the critic wording and the G12 card

blocks.heading: B2: critic redundancy rule
blocks.text: On G12 the critic prompt contradicted itself. Rule 8 keeps an order the task states; rule 6 rejects a redundancy. G12 has a stated "if you move the ball you must also take the key" that the key-before-box order and the goal already imply. luna called it redundant, asked to drop it, then (with deepseek) asked for it back. The fix limits "redundant, reject" to a listed `Existence` and keeps any stated order or "if" rule. With it luna answers: "The conditional clause is redundant but is stated in the task, so it should stay".

- `Redundant`: a hard clause the other hard clauses already imply, so the machine is the
-  same without it. It is a defect on its own: reject and ask to drop it, usually the `Existence`
-  of an earlier step of a `Precedence` chain, and keep the chain and the `Existence` of the last
-  step.
+  same without it. A listed `Existence` is a defect on its own: reject and ask to drop it, usually
+  the `Existence` of an earlier step of a `Precedence` chain, and keep the chain and the `Existence`
+  of the last step. Any other listed clause that a task sentence states, such as an order or an
+  "if" rule, stays: never ask to drop it.
(checklist 6: "One redundancy is worth a rejection" becomes "One redundant `Existence` is worth a rejection")

blocks.heading: B1: G12 card gap
blocks.text: Two runs in arm B ended on `Existence(target_picked_up)` plus hard `Precedence(has_door_key, target_picked_up)`. The card's own answer adds `RespondedExistence(blocker_moved, has_door_key)`. A product of the clause DFAs shows the two sets accept exactly the same runs: the hard order plus the hard goal already force the key. The scorer could not see it. The card now lists that set as an answer, and both box orders as `forced` (the door opens only from the ball's cell and with the key, and the box room has no other entrance).

**Critic set.** Relabelled for stated orders: 30 wrong items, 8 right (was 28 and 10). glm at `medium` catches 28 of 30 on call 1, with 0 of 8 false alarms; the earlier glm `medium` run, relabelled, caught 24 of 30. One run per item, so +4 is a gain, not a precise number.

**Scorer.** `check/chain_score.py` now takes its optional implied orders from every hard `Precedence` of the card, not only the forced ones (key before goal when key before door before goal accepts the same runs). On the runs scored before the audit it gives the same verdicts.

blocks.title: Ran before the shape fix
blocks.text: This sweep ran with the old generator prompt, which never named the JSON shape. The short first proposals below are what that fix removed: at `max` and `high`, 0 short and every first proposal right afterwards. See `docs/paper/hidden-output-schema/`.

items: **The final machine does not depend on the level.** 46 of 46 right at every level; the critic caught every wrong first proposal. Level buys critic recall and costs time.
**Short first proposals are one clause.** 36 of 37 hold a single clause. Cause found later: the generator was never shown the JSON shape (`docs/paper/hidden-output-schema/`).
**Max costs 4.5 times the medium wall time** and two 600 s generator timeouts (G12, third try after about 315 s). Generator calls reach 31,662 output tokens.

**Recommendation: `high` if the default moves.** Same final result as `medium`, 96% of defects flagged on the critic's first call against 81%, for +32% total wall time and about 2.7 times the critic tokens. Not `max`. `CONFIG.reasoning` was not changed.
**Limits.** One run per card and level; the critic sweep used a fixed 21-item subset (16 wrong, 5 right, seed 20261120), so one item either way is noise; `none` was not rerun in loop 2.

**The reasoning default.** The loop recommends `medium` for both roles (46/46 against 42/46, critic catch 14 to 22 of 28, same calls per run, 6 times the wall time). `CONFIG.reasoning` still defaults to `none`; no default was changed. The user decides. Loop 2 later recommends `high` if the default moves (see the sweep).

**Stated orders the level forces.** Every strong critic (luna, Haiku, glm at `medium`) asks for them (s02, w08, w03, r05, G4), while the cards mark them `forced`, optional. Critic rule 8 says to keep them. The decision records (`docs/decisions/arm-fm/task-and-rm-identity.md:109-111`, `rm-execution.md:95-98`) say the critic rejects a clause that restates an environment-guaranteed order. The three disagree. Today it costs extra rounds, not wrong machines. Since settled for the cards: the user rule keeps every stated order (`docs/decisions/` updated in main `9ead827`), and the audit made them required.
**glm at `medium` still accepts 8 of 28 critic-set items with a defect left** (luna 1, Haiku 0). In the pipeline it caught 11 of 12 wrong first proposals.

**Short first proposals at `medium`** (10 of 66). They are safe only while the critic catches them; glm did, 10 of 10. No change made; watch them in the next full run. Cause found and fixed since: the generator was never shown the JSON shape (`docs/paper/hidden-output-schema/`).

**The `none` rerun** of W5a, U5, S2, O7 with the new critic wording was not run (budget). B2 touches only candidates whose clues list a redundant non-`Existence` clause, so no change is expected there.

**`evidence/`** (1.8 MB): `model-compare-report.md` and `llm-loop-report.md` (every number on this page comes from them or from the records below); `items.json` and `items-b2.json` (the 38 critic items and their B2 form); `b1-equiv.txt`; `cards/local-soft/tasks.json`; `model-compare/runs/` and `llm-loop/runs/`: one summary JSON per run (`<round>/<arm>/<case>-r<k>.json`, with status, clauses, trace, machine text, wall time), the `.rm` files of the wrong machines, `round.log` per round (it holds the exact cases, arms and reasoning level), and `explain*.json` (the verdict and nearest card answer of each non-right machine).

**`evidence/llm-loop2/`** (3.2 MB, loop 2): `cards/` (the audited cards the loop scored with), `cards.diff` and `prompt.diff`, `items.json` (the relabelled critic set; `items-old.json` the earlier one), `critic-subset.txt`, `rescore/` (old against new verdicts and the 4 machines turned wrong), `runs/f-{low,medium,high,max}/A` (one summary per run, a slim call log per run with stage, reply, wall time, error and token usage; prompts and schema dropped; `round.log`), `runs/critic/glm-*` (critic-set records without `first_prompt`) and `runs/sweep-table.md`. The report is `evidence/llm-loop2-report.md`.

**Cards pinned.** The repository's cards changed after this entry (the audit, then the card review), so `evidence/cards/{base,complex,templates}/` keeps the cards the first report and loop scored with (main `57f6a1a`). `check/cases.py` reads `CARD_DIR` (default: those pinned cards); `CARD_DIR=docs/paper/model-comparison/evidence/llm-loop2/cards` scores against the audited ones.

**Not copied** (all still in `.git/agent-memory/plans/farm-final-20261119/model-compare-evidence` and `llm-loop-evidence`, about 93 MB): the 434 call logs `*.calls.jsonl` (55.5 MB; they hold seconds per call, tokens and usage), the per-run `.log` files, the `*_work` folders (one per run, 22 MB), the 8 dry runs `p1` (run before the context stripping), the `STOP` marker, `__pycache__`, and the run tools `run_arms.py/.sh`, `run_critic_set.py/.sh`, `critic_cli.py`, `gen_one.py`, `critic_one.py`, `budget*.py`, `explain.py`. The run tools call the models and read the `.env` credentials, so they are not part of a rerun here.

**Edited copy.** The 172 critic-set records had `first_prompt` removed (the whole critic prompt, about 70 KB each, 6.9 MB in all); the other fields are unchanged. The prompts rebuild from `items.json` and the critic prompt in git.

**Numbers that need the call logs:** the calls per arm, seconds per call, and output and reasoning tokens. `arm_stats.py` and `critic_stats.py` print 0 for those columns on the copy; the figures on this page are the ones the loop report printed from the logs.
